message.content: Hey. I need help with the structural logic for my final model. The central atrium is collapsing in the simulation, and I’m running out of time.

content.text: I can pull up the latest parametric data for that section. Are we talking about the load-bearing columns or the roof truss? Also, did you update the material density settings after your café shift yesterday?

message.content: The columns. I updated them, but the stress points are still red. Also, remind me what I said about the internship search last night?

content.text: On Wednesday, March 25th, you mentioned you haven't sorted out a summer internship at an architecture office in Busan yet. You wanted to prioritize firms with sustainable design portfolios.

message.content: Right. That’s still the plan. I can’t let the model fail while I’m worrying about that. Back to the model: if I switch the column material to reinforced concrete instead of steel, does that fix the render?

content.text: It should reduce the weight load significantly. I’ll run a quick test. While that processes, do you want me to draft a quick email to three Busan firms you bookmarked last week? It might help break the cycle of procrastination.

message.content: Yes, please. Just keep it brief. And... thanks. I’m feeling pretty fried today.

content.text: The simulation is done. The concrete columns hold. Also, I noticed you logged a change in your health tracker. You went back to 5 mg for the sleeping pill, not 10 mg. That was on Tuesday, March 24th, correct?

message.content: Yeah, I realized 10 was too much. I just need to sleep, not be out of it. Anyway, send those emails. I have to go to Hongdae Photo Society later for the evening session. It helps me clear my head.

content.text: Emails sent. Good idea to disconnect for a bit. Focus on the photos, not the studio stress. I’ll have the updated model file ready for you when you get back.
